title: Gun or cartridge malfunctions
summary: What to do when the gun does not fire, and how a malfunction is scored in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

body.html: A malfunction is a failure of the gun or cartridge: a misfire, a second barrel that does not fire, or both barrels firing together (double discharge).
After a misfire, stay where you are with the gun closed and pointing down the range until the referee has examined it.
body.heading: Watch what to do after a misfire

body.html: First, what the shooter must do: stay where you are, with the gun pointing down the range. Do not open it or touch the safety until the referee has examined it. Opening the gun or touching the safety first means the target or targets are scored zero. Do not try to take a loaded gun apart on the stand.

Why not open the gun straight away? Occasionally a cartridge fires late, a fraction of a second or longer after the trigger is pulled: a hang fire. If the gun is open or pointing sideways at that moment, that is dangerous. So in training without a referee, wait with the gun pointing safely before you open it; your instructor or the ground's rules will tell you how long.

html.sporting: Per round of 25 targets. The first incident is a No Bird with a warning, and the target is repeated. From the second, the target is not repeated but scored zero.
html.compak: Per round of 25 targets. The first incident is a No Bird with a yellow card. A second of the same kind brings a red card, and targets not shot at are zero.

body.html: Your first malfunction in the round, case by case. (1) The first shot fails: you shoot the single or the double again. If you still fired the second shot, that result counts. (2) On a single, the second shot fails: you shoot it again, and on the repeat only a hit with the second shot counts. So miss with the first shot on purpose. (3) Both barrels go off at once at a single, or at the first target of a double: No Bird, nothing is written down, and you shoot again. How each kind of double is repeated is in the rules guide (Chapter 6 · Malfunction on the second shot).

If your gun is repaired before the squad has finished the stand, you may shoot the stand last, with the referee's permission. If it cannot be repaired, you may switch to another gun at once, with the referee's agreement, or finish later in another squad if the jury allows it. Apart from a malfunction, you may not change your gun, choke or barrels once you are on the stand.

Your first malfunction in the round. If both barrels fire together or the first cartridge fails, the single or double is thrown again, and the failed attempt counts for nothing. If the second cartridge fails on a single, the target is thrown again, but only the second shot can score it. So miss with the first shot on purpose. For doubles, see the rules guide (Chapter 20 · The second cartridge fails).

After a malfunction you have two minutes to get the gun working again or to replace it. As an exception, you may borrow a gun from someone outside your own squad or group, with the owner's and the referee's agreement. Without a working gun, the remaining targets are zero. Otherwise no gun, choke or barrel may be changed within a round.

A rabbit is the clay that rolls along the ground. In both disciplines, if you miss it with the first shot and it then breaks on its own before your second shot, it is a No Bird. This can happen when it hits a stone. On the repeat only the second shot counts, as after a second-shot malfunction.
Check your gun and cartridges before the round, on the test stand near the clubhouse if there is one. Test shots on the shooting stand are not allowed in either discipline.

notes.html: Pass the referee's words on at once and word for word: 'stay there, don't open the gun'. Explain the reasons only after the check.

key_points.html: After a failure, stay put with the gun closed and pointing down the range; opening it before the referee's check costs the target.
First incident in a round: a No Bird and a warning (in Compak® Sporting, a yellow card).

Second incident in the same round: no repeat. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the target is zero. In Compak® Sporting a second failure of the same kind brings a red card, and targets not shot at are zero.
Second shot fails on a single: on the repeat only a hit with the second shot counts.
Compak® Sporting: two minutes to repair the gun or replace it.

did_you_know.html: Some 'malfunctions' at the start are simply a safety catch left on. A coach can teach you to check it before you call.

quiz.q: Your cartridge misfires. What do you do first?

options.text: Open the gun and check the cartridge
Reload at once and call again
Stay put, gun closed, and wait for the referee

quiz.explain: Opening the gun or touching the safety before the referee's check means the target is scored zero.

quiz.q: In Sporting™, a second gun malfunction happens in the same round, on a single. What is the result?
quiz.explain: Only the first malfunction in a round is a No Bird; from the second, the target is scored zero.

quiz.q: How long do you have in Compak® Sporting to repair or replace the gun?
quiz.explain: You have two minutes; without a working gun, the targets not shot are zero.
